newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Implats lifts attributable earnings 17 pct.
newsitem.headline: Implats lifts attributable earnings 17 pct.

text.p: Impala Platinum Holdings Ltd (Implats) said on Thursday it had lifted attributable earnings for the year ended June 30 1997 by 17 percent to 205 million rand from 176 million a year ago.

"Once again, Implats has produced at just over the 1.0 million platinum ounce level which, combined with the small increase in rand prices for the year, resulted in a 14 percent rise in turnover," Implats said in a statement accompanying results.
Earnings per share was 330 cents/share from 282 previously. Analysts polled by Reuters had forecast earnings per share between 311-339 cents.
The company, South Africa's second-largest platinum producer, said an increase in turnover combined with the containment of costs led to a 55 percent increase in mining income.
The company said it increased earnings despite reduced financial income and higher taxes and royalties.
Capital expenditure was relatively stable, it said.
It said tonnage from underground increased by two percent despite a three-day wage strike and underperformance at two shafts.
"Sales volumes for all metals were significantly higher than last year due to better operational performance. The most notable increase was in platinum sales of 992,400 ounces," Implats said.
Capital expenditure was 276 million rand and Implats said it expected capex in the present financial year to be higher at 277 million.
Implats said it was well-positioned to benefit from improved metal prices and to further increase earnings in the present financial year.

"Together with identified working cost initiatives, increased volumes from the mines and our capital efficient decline systems, the company is well positioned to benefit from improved metal prices and to further increase earnings".
